Native functional recovery evidence and descriptive Monte Carlo diagnostics

etr_functional_recovery_evidence.Rd

Independently validated recovery records, per-replicate source metric tables, scenario failure frequency with binomial Monte Carlo standard error, descriptive groupwise recovery summaries, and metric-specific source plots. These methods do not run simulation, fit an estimator, or infer scientific qualification cutoffs.

Usage

etr_functional_recovery_result(records, metric_definitions = list())
etr_functional_recovery_frame(result)
etr_functional_recovery_failure_frame(result)
etr_functional_recovery_summary_frame(result, python_boundary_mode = TRUE)

Arguments

records

Nonempty list of explicit scenario replicate records: scenario_name, replicate (zero-based), seed, status and a named numeric metrics vector. Replicate and seed integers with magnitude below \(2^{53}\) are retained exactly, including values outside R's integer storage range. Successful records require nonempty finite metrics; failed records require no metric values and explicit error_type and error_message. Optional structured metric_values carry metric metadata, source and zero-based component.

metric_definitions

Optional list of uniquely named semantic metric metadata records, with name, quantity, direction, units and scope.

result

Native functional recovery result produced by the constructor; not a Python dataclass.

python_boundary_mode

Use the frozen NumPy double-precision pairwise reductions and linear interpolation arithmetic for the group summary. The default uses R's native arithmetic.

Value

The constructor returns an explicit etr_functional_recovery_result list. The next three methods return tidy numeric R data frames, and the plot function draws base R graphics and invisibly returns exact source x, estimate and interval geometry.

Details

Source alignment is with the published eyetrajectoriespy 1.2.0 FunctionalRecoveryResult and FunctionalRecoveryRecord contracts. Failures are retained in the denominator, not discarded or silently imputed. Failure Monte Carlo standard error is \(\sqrt{p(1-p)/n}\). Group summaries retain sample standard deviation (ddof=1), type-7 linear quantiles matching NumPy's default linear quantiles, median, IQR and standard error of the mean. Source component labels are reported one-based even though structured scientific source values use zero-based component indices. Scenario names and grouped metric keys sort by UTF-8 code point. The explicit Python arithmetic mode preserves source numeric outcomes for cancellation or overflow at extreme finite inputs, including nonfinite computed summaries. Python runtime warning behavior is outside this numerical replay mode.

Monte Carlo summaries are descriptive and impose no automatic qualification, calibrated coverage, or causal interpretation. Python accepts immutable dataclasses and returns pandas tables and Matplotlib Axes; native R uses independently validated lists, data frames and base graphics. Complete public Python source return-class/error equivalence remains unapproved pending independent review of the entire accepted domain.
